title: Conductor-first extension of a normalized resolution from normal quasi-excellent inputs
statement:
Let $N$ assign to every normal reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent scheme $S$ over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-exc-excellent-ring], including finite disjoint unions, a finite tower of normalized blowups [def-trf-normalized-blowup] starting at $S$, with coherent ideal centers whose zero schemes are nonempty and nowhere dense, and with regular last scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Suppose that for every regular morphism $h:T	o S$ between such schemes, meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres, $N(T)$ is canonically the recursively pulled-back tower $h^*N(S)$ with exactly its unit-ideal stages deleted, retaining the other extended ideals in order; that these comparisons respect identities and composition and delete no stage for surjective $h$; and that $N(\varnothing)$ is trivial.

For a reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent $\mathbf Q$-scheme $X$ let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], put $D_X=\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_X}\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal O_X	o
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u})$ [def-trf-conductor-cokernel], where the annihilator consists of local functions killing all local sections, and $P(X)=\operatorname{Bl}_{D_X}(X)^
u$ [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Then $
u$ is finite, $D_X$ is a coherent ideal, $V(D_X)$ is exactly the set of points whose local ring is not an integrally closed domain, this set is nowhere dense, and $D_X=\mathcal O_X$ exactly when $X$ is normal. $P(X)$ is a normal reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent $\mathbf Q$-scheme of finite type over $X$. Define $H_N(X)$ to be $P(X)	o X$, with center $D_X$, followed by $N(P(X))$, omitting the first stage exactly when $D_X=\mathcal O_X$. This is a finite normalized blowup tower with coherent centers having nonempty nowhere dense zero schemes and with regular last scheme; $H_N(\varnothing)$ is trivial.

For every regular morphism $h:Y	o X$ between reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent $\mathbf Q$-schemes, $D_Y=D_X\mathcal O_Y$, $P(Y)\simeq P(X)	imes_XY$ canonically, and $P(Y)	o P(X)$ is regular, surjective if $h$ is. The resulting comparisons identify $H_N(Y)$ with the contraction $(h^*H_N(X))^c$, preserving the ordered extended ideals and respecting identities and composition. A stage is deleted exactly when its extended ideal is the unit ideal, and every deleted stage is an isomorphism; no stage is deleted when $h$ is surjective. Finite disjoint unions are inputs. Noetherian schemes here admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings.

source.place: VIII 2.2.1--2.2.4, Lemma 2.2.9, 2.3.2, 2.3.4 and Remark 2.3.12(i), printed pp.89--94 (normalized blowups, regular base change of normalization, normalized desingularization and its regular functoriality); finiteness of normalization of a quasi-excellent scheme: Stacks Tag 07QV (more-algebra.tex, a quasi-excellent ring is Nagata). The conductor-first form makes the unit-center stages of normalized towers isomorphisms, as in the finite-type smooth version lem-trf-conductor-extension-of-normalized-resolution.

proof.text: For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata] makes $A$ Nagata. By [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], each $A/\mathfrak p_i$ for a minimal prime is N-2 and hence N-1 (take the degree-one field extension). The affine description [lem-per-componentwise-normalization-affine-charts] therefore identifies $\nu^{-1}U$ with the spectrum of a finite product of finite $A/\mathfrak p_i$-modules. Each is finite over $A$, using the same generators, and their finite product is generated by the union of these generators placed in individual coordinates. Thus $\nu$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. This argument applies to every reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent input, and in particular to the ordinary blowup used below.

source.place: Tag 035S, lemma-nagata-normalization, affine proof; Tag 035P, lemma-description-normalization. Finiteness is derived here from the existing affine chart statement and the definition of Nagata.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-normalization-quotient-local-criterion]: the normalization sequence is short exact, $C_X$ is coherent, and $C_{X,x}=0$ exactly when $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is an integrally closed domain. All hypotheses hold: $X$ is reduced and locally Noetherian, and finiteness was established in step 1.

source.place: Tag 07QV, lemma-quasi-excellent-nagata; morphisms.tex 035S, lemma-nagata-normalization; 035P and 0C3B through the cited quotient criterion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-support] to $C_X$. Its annihilator is the quasi-coherent ideal $D_X$, and $V(D_X)=\operatorname{Supp}C_X$, which by step 2 is precisely the nonnormal locus. On each affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$, its ideal is finitely generated since $A$ is Noetherian; hence [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes $D_X$ coherent. The support misses every generic point: the reduced local ring at a minimal prime has only one prime, so its nilradical and maximal ideal are both zero, making it a field; [lem-per-componentwise-normalization-properties](1) identifies the normalization at such a point with its residue-field spectrum, so the quotient stalk is zero. Since the support is closed, this proves nowhere density. Finally $D_X=\mathcal O_X$ iff the support is empty iff all local rings are integrally closed domains. These arguments also apply to every other input, including $Y$.

source.place: Tag 035Q, lemma-normalization-normal, generic fibres; scheme-theoretic-support and coherence are cited separately.

proof.text: Put $W=\operatorname{Bl}_{D_X}X$. By [lem-per-reduced-noetherian-blowup-geometry], $W$ is reduced Noetherian and finite type over $X$. By [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability], it is quasi-excellent. Applying step 1 to $W$ makes $W^\nu\to W$ finite. Therefore $P(X)=W^\nu$ is finite type over $X$: on affine charts a finite algebra is generated as an algebra by any finite module generating set, and composition preserves finite generation by substituting the finite generator lists. The same chart argument gives quasi-compactness. Apply [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability] again to obtain quasi-excellence and Noetherianity of $P(X)$. Its normality follows from [lem-per-componentwise-normalization-properties](1); integrally closed domain stalks are reduced. The structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$ is the composite with that of $X$.

For any normal Noetherian scheme $S$, the unit ideal is invertible; [cor-nagata-blowup-cartier-iso] identifies its ordinary blowup with $S$, and [lem-per-componentwise-normalization-properties](2), applied to $U=S$, identifies its normalization with $S$. Thus a normalized unit-center blowup of a normal scheme is canonically an isomorphism. If $D_X$ is unit, step 3 says $X$ is normal, so $P(X)\simeq X$. Otherwise prepend the stage with center $D_X$ to the finite tower $N(P(X))$. The center is nowhere dense by step 3 and nonempty because a proper stalk ideal lies in the stalk maximal ideal. Step 4 verifies every hypothesis for applying $N$; its tail has the stipulated centers and regular endpoint. The number of stages is one plus the tail length, or the tail length when $D_X$ is unit. On $\varnothing$ the unique ideal is unit, $P(\varnothing)=\varnothing$ by [def-trf-normalized-blowup], and $N(\varnothing)$ is trivial. Finite disjoint unions are within the specified input class and need no synchronization choice in this construction.

source.place: VIII 2.2.3, 2.3.2 and 2.3.4; conductor-prepending assembly, with the unit-normalization distinction explicit.

proof.text: Let $h:Y\to X$ be regular. By [lem-per-normalized-tower-regular-pullback], normalization commutes canonically with $h$. On affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, set $A'=\Gamma(\nu_X^{-1}\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)$. Finiteness from step 1 makes $A'$ finite over $A$. The affine-pushforward comparison [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] and the normalization isomorphism identify the normalization algebra over $B$ with $A'\otimes_A B$, carrying $B$ into it by $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. Flatness of $A\to B$ is [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to the normalization sequence identifies its quotient with $(A'/A)\otimes_A B$. Consequently [lem-trf-annihilator-finite-flat-base-change], with the finite module $A'/A$, gives $D_Y|_{\operatorname{Spec}B}=D_X\mathcal O_Y|_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$. These local equalities give $D_Y=D_X\mathcal O_Y$; tensor associativity and the cited canonical comparisons make the equalities compatible with identity and composition.

source.place: VIII Lemma 2.2.9; Stacks algebra.tex Tag 07T8, lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change; affine pushforward base change and exactness supplied by cited nodes.

proof.text: Apply the recursive normalized-tower comparison [lem-per-normalized-tower-regular-pullback] to the single stage with center $D_X$. Its levels are Noetherian by step 4. Step 6 identifies its extended ideal with $D_Y$, so this gives $\theta_h:P(Y)\simeq P(X)\times_XY$, compatibly with identities and composition. The map $\bar h:P(Y)\to P(X)$ is regular: on finite-type affine charts of $P(X)\to X$, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change] applies to the regular affine ring maps defining $h$ and their finite-type base change; regularity is local in these charts, with flatness read by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] and fibres the same scheme-theoretic fibres. No finite-type hypothesis on $h$ is used. If $h$ is surjective, [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] makes this projection, hence $\bar h$, surjective.

source.place: VIII 2.2.8--2.2.9; Stacks more-algebra.tex Tag 07C1, lemma-regular-base-change, applied only along the finite-type morphism P(X) to X.

proof.text: Compare the initial stage in three cases. If $D_X$ is unit, so is $D_Y$, and neither construction includes it. If both are nonunit, retain the pulled-back stage, identified by $\theta_h$. If $D_X$ is nonunit but $D_Y$ is unit, delete it: $Y$ is normal by step 3, so its normalized unit blowup is an isomorphism by step 5. In all cases the next comparison is the same normal-input map $\bar h$. Apply the hypothesis on $N$ to this regular map between the normal quasi-excellent Noetherian schemes of step 4. Its comparison deletes exactly unit tail centers and keeps all other extended ideals in order. Inductively, the level-zero match is $\theta_h$; if the levels match through index $i$, the next center is the same extended ideal and its normalized blowup is the same construction [def-trf-normalized-blowup], so the next levels match too. Unit stages can be removed without changing subsequent levels: their lower scheme is normal, initially $P(Y)$ and thereafter a normalized blowup, and step 5 applies. This proves the asserted contracted-tower comparison and every deletion assertion.

source.place: VIII 2.2.5--2.2.9, 2.3.4 and 2.3.5(i); explicit finite-list induction using only the given comparison law for N.

proof.text: For $Z\xrightarrow gY\xrightarrow hX$, steps 6--7 identify the normal-input map for $h\circ g$ with $\bar h\circ\bar g$. The hypothesis on $N$ gives equality of the tail comparisons. On center indices, extending twice equals extending once along the composite, and a unit ideal remains unit after extension. Deleting indices already unit over $Y$ and then those becoming unit over $Z$ therefore deletes exactly the indices unit over $Z$, in their original order. The initial-index cases of step 8 obey the same rule. This proves composition of the assembled comparisons. For identity maps the conductor and all levels are unchanged and the comparison for $N$ is the identity, proving the identity law.

source.place: VIII 2.3.4; identity and composition assembly for conductor-prepending and ordered deletion.

proof.text: If $h$ is surjective and $D_X$ is nonunit, choose $x\in V(D_X)$ and $y$ above it. The local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ maps $(D_X)_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x$ into $\mathfrak m_y$, so the extended conductor is proper at $y$. By step 6 it is $D_Y$; the initial stage is retained. Step 7 makes $\bar h$ surjective, so the no-deletion hypothesis for $N$ retains every tail stage. This includes unit $D_X$, when there was no initial stage, and the empty-to-empty case.

source.place: VIII Remark 2.3.5(i); local-ring argument for the conductor index, and the stated surjective comparison hypothesis on N for the tail.

lean.note: The three theorem declarations state the geometry, canonical regular base change, and extension clauses of this one node. The preparation definitions use the actual existing conductor normalized blowup and only named geometric proof fields. IsConductorResolutionExtension identifies all tail levels, arrows and center ideals, and includes the conductor stage exactly when nonunit. No canonical construction is replaced by an arbitrary morphism or an unconstrained existence choice.

QEConductorGeometry covers finite ν, the coherent Ann-coker conductor, support = non-normal locus, nowhere density, unit iff normal, and P(X) normal/reduced/Noetherian/qe/finite type over X. qeConductor_regularBaseChange gives D_Y = comap and the canonical cartesian P-square, regular and surjective when h is; the ∃! over the conjunction is harmless because maps over X into P(X) are unique. IsConductorResolutionExtension pins tail levels, arrows and centers, the conductor stage when nonunit and the unitBase case; H's existential comparisons are forced by uniqueness. Edge cases checked: empty input, length-0 tail, D_X nonunit with D_Y unit, surjective h, disconnected inputs, universes.
